newsitem.title: USA: U.S. official pleased with index-linked note sale.
newsitem.headline: U.S. official pleased with index-linked note sale.

text.p: The Treasury's second auction of inflation-indexed notes was a success, despite the sharp drop-off in bidding demand from the first such sale in January, a Treasury Department official said Tuesday.
"The (second) auction was a success," said the official, who declined to be identified. "January's was a really big success."

The first auction of $7 billion of 10-year inflation-indexed notes on January 29 drew bids of $37.22 billion, or 5.31 times the amount sold. The sale held earlier Tuesday of $8 billion of 9-3/4-year inflation-indexed notes -- a reopening of the first issue -- drew only $18.06 billion of bids, or 2.26 times the amount sold.
Despite the lower level of bids, the official said the 2.26 bid-to-cover ratio was "right in the middle" of the average of 10-year note auctions over the past three years.
"We certainly never expected to match the success of January," the official said.

Expressing satisfaction with the latest results, the official said the new note, which is designed to protect its holders from inflation, is seen by the Treasury as a long-term project, especially in attracting retail buyers.
"The whole development of the market is a long-term project for us," the official said. "But retail market takes even longer."
In the latest auction, non-competitive bids from individual investors fell to $36 million from $157 million in January.
